MY STORY ADVENTURE

Where Is My Story?

Imagine a place and choose details that help someone picture it.

Look, then try.

The treehouse, castle and spaceship are starting ideas. Your setting can be real or imaginary. Think about the time of day, what your character sees and what sounds they notice. Choose a detail that matters to the story, such as a locked door or a hidden path.

Start drawing and writing below

Open the worksheet to print or save

An adult helps cut character cards. Keep small paper scraps away from younger children. You can draw, type or ask a grown-up to write your words.

Use a finger, stylus or mouse in each drawing box. Type below it, or ask a grown-up to write your words. Your work stays in this tab. Save before refreshing or leaving.

ACTIVITY 1

My story place

Draw the setting, leaving room for the details you want to describe.

ACTIVITY 2

A useful detail

Draw one part of the setting that affects what happens.

Your ideas belong here. There is no score.

What are we learning?

Setting tells us where and when events happen. Specific details make a story easier to imagine.
